subject.title: [Bug] Webchat avatar endpoint /avatar/{agentId} returns 404 even with valid IDENTITY.md avatar

question: Should local avatar failures keep generic direct-route 404s with clearer authenticated UI/metadata diagnostics, or should `/avatar/{agentId}` itself expose more specific missing/oversized failure statuses?
rationale: The remaining behavior affects authenticated local workspace file serving, so better UX must be balanced against information-disclosure and path-policy boundaries.

options.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
options.body: Keep direct image fetches generic while using existing metadata reasons and UI surfaces to explain oversized, missing, or rejected local avatars.

options.title: Expose Specific Route Errors
options.body: Return statuses such as 413 or 400 from the avatar route after explicit security review and tests proving no unsafe path details leak.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Avatar Contract
options.body: Defer this local diagnostics choice into the broader Control UI avatar contract tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/41201.

recommendation.title: Improve UI Diagnostics Only
recommendation.body: Keep direct image fetches generic while using existing metadata reasons and UI surfaces to explain oversized, missing, or rejected local avatars.

likelyOwner.reason: The avatar route, resolver, and hardening history point most strongly to this owner path for the security-boundary choice.
